edges.description: Repeated sinopulmonary infection produced bronchiectasis in both siblings.

Both siblings' glomerulonephritis was post-streptococcal, with a raised anti-streptolysin O titre. The original authors suggest it may be secondary to the infection burden rather than attributable to RAC2 loss, so this edge records the infection route alongside the immune-dysregulation one.
Chemotaxis, L-selectin-mediated capture under shear and F-actin generation are all defective, which is a finer dissection of this node than the single chemotaxis assay available in the patients.
edges.limitations: The mouse does not reproduce the glomerulonephritis, coagulopathy or endocrine features of the human siblings, so the immune-dysregulation arm of the disease has no counterpart in it.

nodes.description:
The mechanism predicts this step: p67phox requires RacGTP binding to undergo the conformational change that lets it engage NOX2, so without membrane-targeted RAC2-GTP the oxidase should not assemble.
How far it is realised in a patient is not settled, and the evidence points both ways. The proband's nitroblue tetrazolium test was normal, which is a direct human measurement against a complete oxidative-burst failure. In the null mouse the result is compartment-dependent: superoxide production was significantly reduced in bone-marrow neutrophils but normal in activated peritoneal exudate neutrophils. So a reduced respiratory burst is expected from the biochemistry and partly seen in the mouse, rather than demonstrated in these patients.

nodes.description: Both siblings developed post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, diagnosed on the clinical picture with a raised anti-streptolysin O titre. In the proband it progressed to end-stage renal disease requiring transplantation, and she died of graft rejection at 21. Whether it is attributable to RAC2 loss or is a consequence of the infection burden is unresolved, and the original authors favour the latter; both routes are recorded as edges.

nodes.description: Glomerulonephritis, factor XI deficiency, urticaria and multiple hormone abnormalities of possible autoimmune basis were present in both siblings. Both glomerulonephritides were post-streptococcal with a raised anti-streptolysin O titre, and the original authors suggest they may be secondary to the infection burden rather than to the genotype; a sequela edge from the recurrent infections records that alternative route. This is the least supported step in the chain: no mechanistic study connects RAC2 loss to renal, coagulation or endocrine pathology, the Rac2-null mouse does not reproduce it, and the original authors themselves suggest some of these features may be secondary to infection or autoimmunity rather than directly attributable.

nodes.description: RAC2 is the downstream effector of the lymphocyte guanine-nucleotide-exchange module, so antigen-receptor, chemokine-receptor and integrin signals lose their Rac-dependent cytoskeletal and transcriptional output. Thymocyte development and B cell development both suffer, which is read out in the patients as reduced T cell receptor excision circles and reduced kappa-deleting recombination excision circles.

nodes.description: The genotype matches the human disease: a constitutional biallelic null in a haematopoietic-restricted gene. It dissects the migration branch in detail, separating chemotaxis, shear-dependent capture and F-actin generation, and shows that the baseline defect becomes lethal only on pathogen challenge.
The presenting clinical feature in both siblings, from six months and two years of age respectively, progressing to bronchiectasis in both.

nodes.description: Coagulation factor XI deficiency with activity below 1% in both siblings, at two and ten years of age. F11 was sequenced and excluded in the proband, so this is not a second independent Mendelian condition segregating in the family. How RAC2 loss produces it is unknown, and the original authors place it among the features that may not be directly attributable.

nodes.description: Levothyroxine for the autoimmune hypothyroidism documented in both siblings with anti-thyroid-peroxidase antibodies. It treats one of the endocrine consequences rather than the immunodeficiency, and is here because the hormone abnormalities are part of this disease's described phenotype and are the kind of thing that goes unlooked-for in a patient being managed as an antibody deficiency.
